title: The Holly and the Ivy
description: The English carol as Cecil Sharp noted it from Mrs Mary Clayton of Chipping Campden and printed it in English Folk-Carols (1911), for 2 to 4 singers: the first three verses, the holly, its white blossom and its red berry, each with the refrain "The rising of the sun". A gentle three, with the alto in thirds and sixths under the tune.

credits.words: Traditional English (as printed by Cecil Sharp, 1911)
credits.tune: Traditional English, as sung by Mrs Mary Clayton of Chipping Campden (noted and printed by Cecil Sharp, 1911)

licence.words: public domain: traditional; printed by Cecil Sharp (died 1924), who notes that he supplemented Mrs Clayton's words with a set recited to him by the late Mrs Wyatt of East Harptree, Somerset, and changed one line of the second stanza to the usual broadside reading ("To be our sweet Saviour")
licence.tune: public domain: traditional, as sung by Mrs Mary Clayton at Chipping Campden and noted by Cecil Sharp (died 1924)
licence.arrangement: original, written for Stackapella: our own four parts under Sharp's tune; Sharp's piano accompaniment (public domain: Sharp died 1924), written for the piano and often over a held G (under "The holly and the" and under "sun"), was read but not copied, and our chords are our own; Sharp's tune as printed, except that the notes before the three breaths give up three quarters of a beat on "grown" and "deer" and a quarter on "crown", where Sharp's printed rest makes up the breath; breaths written in for beginners; under "hol-ly" and "ri-sing" at the start of each verse and refrain the alto sings E4 and the bass holds G2, an E minor chord over G, so the duet has a third where it would otherwise sing a bare fourth.
licence.source: Cecil J. Sharp, English Folk-Carols, with pianoforte accompaniment and an introduction and notes, collected in various parts of England (London: Novello & Co. and Simpkin & Co.; Taunton: Barnicott and Pearce, the Wessex Press; MCMXI, 1911, title page at leaf n6), No. VII, "The Holly and the Ivy", pp. 17 and 18 (music, voice and piano, Andante moderato, verse 1 under the music, all six stanzas printed on p. 18), and the note to No. 7 on pp. 63 and 64 ("Sung by Mrs. Mary Clayton, at Chipping Campden"); in G, 3/4, written here in G in 3/4 as printed; verses 1 to 3 and the refrain as printed, verses 2 and 3 fitted to the notes by us ("li-ly" on two quavers of the high E, "sweet" on one crotchet where verse 1 has "that are", "For to" on the two quavers Sharp slurs for "The"); New York Public Library copy, read from the scan at archive.org/details/englishfolkcarol00shar/page/n34 and n35 (the note: n80 and n81)
